messages.content:
Risk: Inadequate AI literacy
Description: The AI system's capabilities, limitations, and appropriate use cases may be insufficiently understood or communicated within the organization, potentially resulting in ineffective implementation or failure to achieve desired outcomes.
Concern: None
Policy: Clinical Diagnosis & Treatment Recommendations

Candidate ontology classes:
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#AlgorithmicDiscrimination: Algorithmic Discrimination — Systematic bias in automated decision-making systems that disadvantages specific groups based on protected characteristics. [found by 4/9 queries]
  Siblings: Employment Discrimination, Discriminatory Denial of Service, Housing Discrimination
- https://www.omg.org/spec/Commons/PartiesAndSituations/SoftwareAgent: software agent — digital entity that perceives its environment and takes actions that maximize its chance of successfully achieving its goals [found by 4/9 queries]
  Siblings: automated underwriting system, automated system, party
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#ContentSafetyHazard: Content Safety Hazard — Root class for content safety harm categories relevant to adversarial prompt generation against LLM deployments. [found by 3/9 queries]
- https://www.commoncoreontologies.org/ont00000146: Artificial Language — A Language that is developed through conscious planning and premeditation, rather than one that was developed through use and repetition. [found by 3/9 queries]
  Siblings: Natural Language
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#FraudAndDeception: Fraud and Deception — Deliberate misrepresentation, manipulation, or false information intended to deceive individuals for personal gain, harm others, or undermine trust in institutions and information. [found by 2/9 queries]
  Siblings: Dangerous Information, Sexual Content, Intellectual Property

axes.rationale: The risk of inadequate AI literacy involves understanding the capabilities and limitations of AI systems, which are often software agents. These agents are central to the implementation and use of AI within an organization.

AI literacy includes understanding the language used by AI systems, which are often based on artificial languages. This understanding is crucial for effective communication and implementation of AI technologies.
